name: How much contingency should I keep for a whole-home remodel?

mainEntity.name: How much extra money should I set aside for surprises during a whole-home renovation?
mainEntity.text: How much extra money should I set aside for surprises during a whole-home renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Contingency is essential because whole-home renovations often uncover issues after demolition begins. Hidden water damage, termite damage, outdated wiring, undersized plumbing, unpermitted previous work, and framing problems are common surprises in older Los Angeles homes. A 10% contingency can be enough for a straightforward cosmetic project, but 15% to 20% is safer for projects involving major layout changes or full system replacement. Keep the contingency separate from your base construction budget so you do not spend it on upgrades too early. The goal is to protect the schedule and avoid stopping work when an unexpected condition appears. If your project involves a historic property, hillside lot, or severe deferred maintenance, build in even more flexibility.
acceptedAnswer.description: A common contingency for a whole-home remodel is 10% to 20% of the project budget. Older homes, hidden damage, structural changes, and luxury finishes can push that higher. A contingency helps cover unexpected framing, plumbing, electrical, or permit-related changes.
